claims.text: Asthma exacerbation: add to a beta-2 agonist, not first-line alone; can share the albuterol nebulizer.
claims.quote: Ipratropium should be added to beta-2 agonists and not used as first-line therapy. It may be mixed in same nebulizer as albuterol.
claims.locator: Table: Pharmacologic Treatment of Asthma Exacerbations › Ipratropium › Comments

claims.text: Adult dose 0.5 mg nebulized every 20 min × 3, then every 2–4 h as needed.
claims.quote: 0.5 mg every 20 minutes for 3 doses, then every 2–4 hours as needed
claims.locator: Table: Pharmacologic Treatment of Asthma Exacerbations › Ipratropium › Dosage in Adults

claims.text: Asthma: added to ICS or ICS/LABA it improved lung function and cut exacerbations;
claims.quote: In patients with asthma, clinical trials of tiotropium added to either inhaled glucocorticoids or to a combination of an inhaled long-acting beta-2 agonist plus an inhaled glucocorticoid showed improved pulmonary function and decreased asthma exacerbations compared to placebo (4).

claims.text: triple ICS/LABA/LAMA is recommended for step 5 (severe persistent) in adults.
claims.quote: Inhaled combination therapy with glucocorticoids, long-acting beta-2 agonists, and long-acting muscarinic antagonists are recommended for the maintenance treatment of asthma for severe persistent asthma (step 5) in adults (1).

claims.text: CI: hypersensitivity to ipratropium or to atropine or its derivatives.
claims.quote: Hypersensitivity to ipratropium bromide or other ATROVENT HFA components Hypersensitivity to atropine or any of its derivatives

claims.text: Not for initial treatment of acute bronchospasm needing rapid rescue.
claims.quote: Not indicated for the initial treatment of acute episodes of bronchospasm where rescue therapy is required for rapid response ( 5.1 )
Ocular effects: Use with caution in patients with narrow-angle glaucoma

claims.text: and in prostatic hyperplasia or bladder-neck obstruction (urinary retention);
claims.quote: Urinary retention: Use with caution in patients with prostatic hyperplasia or bladder-neck obstruction

claims.text: can cause life-threatening paradoxical bronchospasm, so stop it if that occurs.
claims.quote: ATROVENT HFA can produce paradoxical bronchospasm that can be life threatening. If this occurs, treatment with ATROVENT HFA should be stopped and other treatments considered.

claims.text: Other anticholinergic drugs: additive anticholinergic effects; avoid the combination.
claims.quote: Anticholinergics: May interact additively with concomitantly used anticholinergic medications. Avoid administration of COMBIVENT RESPIMAT with other anticholinergic-containing drugs (7.1)

claims.text: Prime with 2 test sprays before first use and if unused > 3 days.
claims.quote: Patients should "prime" or actuate ATROVENT HFA before using for the first time by releasing 2 test sprays into the air away from the face. In cases where the inhaler has not been used for more than 3 days, prime the inhaler again by releasing 2 test sprays into the air away from the face.

claims.text: Don't spray into the eyes: it can cause eye pain, blurred vision, halos, mydriasis, or precipitate/worsen narrow-angle glaucoma; see a clinician at once if these occur.
claims.quote: Caution patients to avoid spraying the aerosol into their eyes and be advised that this may result in precipitation or worsening of narrow-angle glaucoma, mydriasis, increased intraocular pressure, acute eye pain or discomfort, temporary blurring of vision, visual halos or colored images in association with red eyes from conjunctival and corneal congestion.

claims.text: Acute inhaled overdose is unlikely: ipratropium is poorly absorbed systemically.
claims.quote: Acute overdose by inhalation is unlikely since ipratropium bromide is not well absorbed systemically after inhalation or oral administration.

claims.text: Maintenance only, not a rescue inhaler: use a rapid-acting beta-2 agonist for acute attacks.
claims.quote: SPIRIVA RESPIMAT is intended as a once-daily maintenance treatment for COPD and asthma and should not be used for the relief of acute symptoms, i.e., as rescue therapy for the treatment of acute episodes of bronchospasm. In the event of an acute attack, a rapid-acting beta 2 -agonist should be used.

claims.text: Renally excreted: with CrCl < 60 mL/min, monitor closely for anticholinergic side effects.
claims.quote: As a predominantly renally excreted drug, patients with moderate to severe renal impairment (creatinine clearance of <60 mL/min) treated with SPIRIVA RESPIMAT should be monitored closely for anticholinergic side effects
